```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(RdistNN)
```

`plqr_dnn()` evaluates localized quantile-score moments at a **supplied
coefficient vector**. It does not solve for coefficients. This guide shows
how moment uncertainty differs from density-backed coefficient uncertainty;
the entire PLQR interface remains experimental.

For statistical background, see the
[paper](https://jakobjuergens.com/research/#orthogonal-inference-conditional-z).
For the supported CATE, regression and CLATE workflows, use
[Getting started](getting-started.html) and [Conditional LATE](conditional-late.html).

## Supply the predictions and coefficient

The demo provides oracle nuisance values. In an application, supply aligned
external predictions: `g` is the model's shape component, `mD` contains the
regressor means, and `density` is the conditional outcome density at the
threshold `D' theta_eval + g`. Nuisance fitting is external.

This example requests both the full moment covariance and a density-backed
coefficient sandwich with `theta_meat = "jackknife"`:

```{r plqr}
demo <- plqr_demo_data(n = 160, p = 2, p_d = 2, tau = 0.5, seed = 1)
fit <- plqr_dnn(
  data = demo$data, x_cols = c("X1", "X2"),
  D_cols = c("D1", "D2"), g_col = "g_oracle",
  mD_cols = c("mD1", "mD2"), y_col = "Y",
  density_col = "density_oracle", theta_eval = demo$truth$theta_true,
  tau = 0.5, x0 = c(0, 0), k = 1L, s = 10L,
  theta_meat = "jackknife", se = TRUE
)

data.frame(
  supplied_coefficient = as.numeric(coef(fit)),
  moment = as.numeric(fit$moment),
  moment_se = as.numeric(fit$moment_se),
  coefficient_se = as.numeric(fit$theta_se)
)
```

The two SE columns have different units. `moment_se` describes variation in
the localized score; `theta_se` additionally uses the density-backed
Jacobian. A small moment is not an estimated coefficient. `coef(fit)` repeats
`theta_eval`, and intervals are centered at that supplied value:

```{r intervals}
confint(fit)
```

Without a density input, leave `theta_meat` at its default and use the fit
for moment diagnostics only; coefficient intervals are unavailable. With a
density input, the default `theta_meat = "analytic"` uses analytic score
covariance. See `?plqr_dnn` for the two sandwich routes and returned arrays.

## Inspect conditioning and new profiles

A well-conditioned regressor Gram matrix does not guarantee a well-conditioned
density-weighted Jacobian. Inspect both:

```{r conditioning}
d <- as.data.frame(diagnostics(fit))
d[, c("target_id", "gram_condition_number", "jacobian_condition_number",
      "theta_vcov_available")]
```

Prediction relocalizes the retained sample. It repeats the supplied
coefficient and computes new uncertainty; it does not fit a new PLQR root.
Prediction uncertainty uses the analytic sandwich even when the original
fit used jackknife meat.

```{r prediction}
pred <- predict(fit, X0 = rbind(c(0, 0), c(0.25, -0.25)), se.fit = TRUE)
pred$se.fit
```

For array shapes and scales, see [Notation and conventions](notation-and-conventions.html).
For the optional conditioning and calibration plots, see `?plot_conditioning`
and `?plot_calibration`. Intervals are pointwise; numerical conditioning does
not verify nuisance accuracy, localization bias or the paper's assumptions.
